speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Inability to pass meconium, Abdominal distension. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is incorrect; migraines do not present with bilious vomiting or failure to pass meconium in an infant. While we wait for the abdominal X-ray results, has your baby been passing any gas or stool since birth, and do you notice any abdominal tenderness when touched? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dilated loops of bowel with no gas in the rectum, suggestive of a distal obstruction.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Intestinal Atresia (likely Jejunal or Ileal Atresia). The combination of bilious vomiting, failure to pass meconium, and an abdominal X-ray showing dilated loops with no gas in the rectum strongly indicates a distal intestinal obstruction atresia rather than malrotation.
